newsitem.title: USA: Big B rejects offer, explores possible sale.
newsitem.headline: Big B rejects offer, explores possible sale.

text.p: Big B Inc said Monday it has rejected an offer from a Revco D.S. Inc subsidiary to acquire all of its outstanding shares of common stock, calling the offer inadequate and not in its best interests.
Revco had offered to pay $15.00 a share in cash.

However, Big B said it has decided to actively explore alternatives to maximize shareholder value. It has said it has already received inquiries from other interested parties, who were not identified.
The company's board of directors has authorized Big B to provide confidential information to interested parties who enter into a confidentiality agreement.
The company said it has made no decision to sell the company but will consider appropriate offers.
Big B also said it has adopted a shareholder rights plan to distribute, as a dividend, one right for each share of common stock held by shareholders of record on October 3.

Under certain circumstances, if an individual or group were to acquire 10 percent or more of the company, or otherwise tried to gain control of the company, the rights would allow stockholders to acquire discount shares of common stock.
The rights plan is to expire June 30, 1997, or earlier under certain circumstances not specified by the company.
Big B is a drug store chain in the southeastern United States.
Revco had said earlier this month, when it increased its bid from $14-a-share to $15-a-share, that it expected the deal would cost $332 million to complete, including fees and related expenses.
Big B said Monday that it rejected the offer in part because of advice from Robinson-Humphrey Corp Inc, its financial adviser, that it was financially inadequate.
A Revco spokesman did not immediately return a telephone call from Reuters seeking comment.
